title: Python Iterables and Iterators
learningObjectives: Explain the main ideas in python iterables and iterators.
Use the relevant iterator or generator protocol correctly.
Trace values and state across successive iteration steps.
Recognize exhaustion, lazy evaluation and relevant edge cases.
Apply the concept to a practical sequence-processing task.

understand.concept: An iterable is an object from which Python can obtain an iterator. An iterator produces values one at a time and remembers its current position. Lists, tuples, strings, sets and dictionaries are iterable, but an iterable container is not necessarily itself an iterator.
understand.whyItMatters: Iteration is the common mechanism behind for loops, comprehensions, unpacking and many data-processing tools. Distinguishing containers from iterators helps explain why some objects can be traversed repeatedly while a particular iterator is consumed.
understand.analogy: An iterable is like a playlist, while an iterator is like a playback cursor that remembers which track comes next.
understand.analogyLimit: A Python iterator is an object implementing a protocol, not a literal cursor stored inside every container. Some iterables are lazy or generate values dynamically rather than holding them all.

explain.narrative:
## Iterable versus iterator
An iterable supports the iterator protocol entry point: `iter(value)` can obtain an iterator from it. An iterator implements `__iter__()` and `__next__()`. Calling `next(iterator)` returns the next value and advances its state. When no values remain, it signals completion with `StopIteration`.

## Reusable containers and one-pass iterators
A list can usually produce a fresh iterator each time `iter(list_value)` is called. A generator object is an iterator and is normally consumed once. After it is exhausted, calling `next()` again continues to raise `StopIteration`.

## for loops
A `for` loop obtains an iterator from the iterable, repeatedly requests values, and stops when iteration is exhausted. This is why the same loop works with lists, strings, dictionaries, files and generators.

practise.guidedTask: Write a small program that demonstrates python iterables and iterators. Show at least two iteration steps and explain how the state changes.
practise.independentTask: Build a reusable or one-pass sequence processor using this topic. Test normal input, an empty or exhausted case, and describe when each value is calculated.

questions.prompt: What does iter(values) return for a list?
questions.explanation: iter asks the object for an iterator; it does not copy the list or return its first value.

questions.prompt: Which protocol method returns the next item?
questions.explanation: An iterator's __next__ method returns one value or raises StopIteration when exhausted.

questions.prompt: What does a for loop do with an iterable?
questions.answer: Obtains an iterator and requests values until exhaustion
options: Obtains an iterator and requests values until exhaustion
Converts every iterable to a list first
Always restarts the iterable after each item
questions.explanation: The iterator protocol underlies Python's for loop.

questions.prompt: Which object is normally consumed as it is iterated?
questions.explanation: A generator object is an iterator with state; once exhausted it does not automatically restart.

questions.prompt: What signals that an iterator has no more values?
questions.explanation: StopIteration is the protocol signal used to end iteration.
